question:
Assertion (A): The value of the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{vmatrix}$ is zero.

Reason (R): If three rows (or columns) of a determinant are in arithmetic progression, then the value of the determinant is zero.
explanation:
Compute the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 8 & 9\end{vmatrix}$.
The rows follow arithmetic progression patterns.
This leads to linear dependence between rows.
When rows of a determinant are linearly dependent, the determinant becomes zero.
Thus the assertion is true.
The reason correctly explains that rows in arithmetic progression lead to determinant zero.
Hence both Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
